findings.statement: In SST zero-shot classification, ablating the sentiment direction removes 76% of above-chance accuracy, and 36% (nearly half of that loss) comes from ablating the summarized direction only at comma positions.

findings.quote: 76% of above-chance classification accuracy is lost when ablating the sentiment direction, nearly half of which (36%) is due to ablating the summarized sentiment direction exclusively at comma positions

findings.statement: Causal interventions isolate the sentiment direction and show it is causally relevant in both toy tasks and real-world datasets such as Stanford Sentiment Treebank.
findings.question: q.tigges2023
findings.quote: Through causal interventions, we isolate this direction and show it is causally relevant in both toy tasks and real world datasets such as Stanford Sentiment Treebank.

source.title: Linear Representations of Sentiment in Large Language Models
source.scope: pythia-1.4b, GPT2-small on ToyMovieReview and SST

tests.description: Directional activation patching along each direction (best layer) in pythia-1.4b, evaluated on ToyMovieReview with out-of-sample adjectives and on SST, measuring mean logit difference and % logit flips.
tests.metric: mean logit difference; % logit differences flipped
tests.quote: Unsupervised methods such as K-means are still able to shift the logit differences and DAS is able to completely flip the prediction.

tests.description: Validate toy-trained DAS direction on SST: binary labels, test partition, subset where pythia-1.4b has 100% zero-shot accuracy (17% removed), 460 clean/corrupted pairs of equal token length, prompt 'Review Text: TEXT, Review Sentiment:', patch the direction in a single layer.
tests.metric: logit flip rate (logit difference Positive vs Negative)
tests.quote: we can flip the output 53.5% of the time (Figure 4).

tests.description: Directional patching of toy-trained directions across layers evaluated on SST test partition, with suffix 'Overall the movie was very' and logit difference good vs bad.
tests.quote: it is in intermediate layers of the model where we see the strongest out-of-distribution performance to SST.

tests.description: Activation addition: add multiples of the sentiment direction to first-layer residual stream of GPT2-small while generating completions from a positive movie review prompt; GPT-4 labels sentiment of outputs.
tests.metric: GPT-4 sentiment labels of generated outputs by steering coefficient
tests.quote: By adding increasingly negative multiples of the sentiment direction, we find that indeed the completions become increasingly negative, without completely destroying the coherence of the model’s generated text.

tests.description: Compute change in sentiment activation at negated tokens between layers 1 and 10 of GPT2-small on 27 negation examples for each direction.
tests.metric: flip percent and median flip size
tests.quote: We made a dataset of 27 negation examples and compute the change in sentiment activation at the negated token (e.g. doubt) between the 1st and 10th layers of GPT2-small.

findings.statement: The mechanisms involving the sentiment direction rely on a small subset of attention heads and neurons.
findings.question: q.tigges2023
findings.quote: We further uncover the mechanisms that involve this direction, highlighting the roles of a small subset of attention heads and neurons.

findings.statement: Across a range of models, sentiment is represented linearly: a single direction in activation space mostly captures the feature across tasks, with positive at one extreme and negative at the other.
findings.question: q.tigges2023
findings.quote: across a range of models, sentiment is represented linearly: a single direction in activation space mostly captures the feature across a range of tasks with one extreme for positive and the other for negative

source.title: Linear Representations of Sentiment in Large Language Models
source.scope: GPT2-small and pythia models (1.4b, 2.8b; GPT-2 medium/large/XL in appendix) on ToyMovieReview, OpenWebText, SST, Harry Potter text

tests.description: Fit sentiment directions (mean difference, K-means, logistic regression probe, DAS, PCA) on ToyMovieReview adjective residual-stream activations in GPT2-small layer 1 and compare them by cosine similarity.
tests.quote: finding extremely high cosine similarity between the learned sentiment directions (Figure 2)

tests.description: Project residual stream activations onto the K-means direction (trained on 30 positive and 30 negative adjectives) and visualize on OpenWebText samples and French Harry Potter text.
tests.data: OpenWebText samples; opening of Harry Potter in French
tests.quote: the extreme values along this direction appear readily interpretable in the wild in diverse text domains such as the opening paragraphs of Harry Potter in French (Figure 1).

tests.description: Bin first-layer GPT2-small K-means sentiment activations of OpenWebText tokens into 20 equal-width buckets, sample 20 tokens per bucket, have GPT-4 label Positive/Neutral/Negative; also classify top/bottom 0.1% activations as positive/negative for each direction method.
tests.quote: the left side area is dominated by the “Negative” label, whereas the right side area is dominated by the “Positive” label and the central area is dominated by the “Neutral” label.

tests.description: 2-means classification accuracy on hold-out adjectives, out-of-distribution verbs and a simple adverbs dataset across layers of GPT-2 small/medium/large/XL; also 2-D PCA clustering of adjective and verb embeddings.
tests.quote: even on hold-out adjectives and on the verb tokens (which are totally out of distribution), we find that the accuracy is generally very strong across models.

tests.description: Sweep DAS subspace dimension (d=2^(n-1)) in GPT2-small and check in-sample and out-of-distribution patching metric.
tests.data: toy movie review dataset (train); simple character mood dataset (validation)
tests.quote: whilst increasing the DAS dimension improves the patching metric in-sample (6(a)), the metric does not improve out-of-distribution (6(b)).

findings.statement: Sentiment is not only represented on emotionally charged words but is also summarized at intermediate positions without inherent sentiment, such as punctuation and names; the authors term this the summarization motif.
findings.question: q.tigges2023
findings.quote: sentiment is not solely represented on emotionally charged words, but is additionally summarized at intermediate positions without inherent sentiment, such as punctuation and names
